title: --incomplete overrides a fail verdict and any threshold
detail: decide() returns abstain for any receipt marked incomplete before it looks at the verdict or counts. Reproduced: `receipt --verdict fail --high 3 --threshold high --incomplete`, then `check --threshold high`, gives decision abstain. A review that already found blocking issues stops blocking as soon as one category was skipped, and the w-review closing step tells the agent to add --incomplete in exactly that case. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js:73.
fix_hint: Check failsThreshold() first and block on a fail verdict or findings at or above the threshold even when the receipt is incomplete; abstain on incomplete only when the recorded findings would not block.

title: Change id covers uncommitted edits, which a push does not send
detail: The id hashes HEAD's tree plus the uncommitted diff and the untracked files. A review run over uncommitted fixes records a receipt for HEAD+fixes. If the developer then pushes without committing those fixes, check sees the same dirty id and abstains, even though the pushed commits (HEAD only) were never reviewed in that form. That is a wrong pass for the input the gate exists to judge. Same code at .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js:256.
fix_hint: For check, key on what is pushed (base + HEAD tree) and treat a dirty tree as unreviewed, or have check refuse to abstain while the tree is dirty.

title: Documented receipt command never sets --threshold, so a threshold check always denies
detail: The closing step records receipts without --threshold, so every receipt is stored under 'none'. decide() blocks whenever the receipt's threshold differs from the check's (push-gate.js:274), so `check --threshold high|medium|low` denies even a 0/0/0 pass. Its message says to run /w-review again, and that writes the same 'none' receipt, so the user can never clear it. The threshold feature cannot be used through the workflow that is meant to feed it. The same text is in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js:2260.
fix_hint: Add `[--threshold <level>]` to the closing-step command and say the check must use the same level. Or store counts without a threshold and judge them against the threshold given at check time.

title: Unknown flags are silently accepted
detail: parse() stores any --key value. A typo such as `check --treshold high` is ignored, so the check falls back to threshold none and gives 'ask' where a 'deny' (exit 2) was intended, with no error.
fix_hint: Allow only known flags for each subcommand (receipt: verdict/high/medium/low/threshold/incomplete/base; check: threshold/base) and throw KitExit 1 on any other flag.

title: Regenerated command file now holds literal backslash-escaped backticks
detail: Regenerating from the dot-shortcuts template wrote `\`` sequences into the markdown (lines 96, 100, 112, 115, 125 and the RC-A block at 144/152). The RC-A example is therefore no longer a fenced code block, and inline commands are no longer code spans. The regeneration also changed the build-phase browser check (it dropped 'Verify responsive layout, dark mode, accessibility'), which is outside this stream's scope.
fix_hint: Fix the over-escaped `\\\`` in the w-review template in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js, then regenerate. Or limit this commit to the closing-step hunk.

title: Closing-step command contains a literal `pass|fail`
detail: If the command is pasted or run as written, the shell reads `pass|fail` as a pipe into a `fail` command and the receipt is not recorded. The placeholders `<H>` are also shell redirections. The same text is in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js:2258.
fix_hint: Show two concrete forms (`--verdict pass` / `--verdict fail`) or write the placeholders as `VERDICT`, `H`, `M`, `L` in prose.

title: Weak or dead assertions in the receipt-history tests
detail: 'keeps the previous change ids' only checks that previous is an array; it never checks that an earlier id was pushed, deduplicated or capped at MAX_PREVIOUS. The unused `receipts`/`void receipts` (809, 816) and the `f`/`other` placeholders in the corrupt-store test (794-799) are dead code.
fix_hint: Check that previous contains the earlier change id, excludes the latest, and is capped at 50; remove the unused variables.

title: Store path is wrong when run from a subdirectory: receipt/check fail with a raw ENOENT or read the wrong store
detail: storeFile() resolves `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` against --show-toplevel, but git prints that path relative to the cwd (from <repo>/sub it prints '../.git'). Resolving it against the toplevel gives <parent>/.git. I reproduced this: `push-gate check` run from a subdirectory exits 1 with 'kit: ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath /tmp/pgt/.git'. That is an uncaught non-KitExit error with a misleading message, so neither receipt nor check works from any subdirectory. If the parent directory happens to have a .git, the gate keys a different store: a receipt recorded at the repo root is then reported as 'no review recorded' from the subdirectory (also reproduced). Mirrored at .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js:158. No test covers running from a subdirectory.
fix_hint: Use `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, as workingTree() already does for --git-path, or resolve the path against the cwd instead of the toplevel. Add a test that records a receipt at the root and runs check from a subdirectory.

title: A missing or unspawnable git is reported as 'not inside a git repository'
detail: defaultGit maps a spawn failure (r.error set, status null, for example ENOENT when git is not on PATH) to code 1 with empty stderr and drops r.error. changeId's first probe then throws 'not inside a git repository', which sends the user the wrong way. Mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/push-gate.js.
fix_hint: When r.error is set, return or throw its message (for example, KitExit(`cannot run git: ${r.error.message}`)).

title: Receipt store update is an unlocked read-modify-write, and a failed write leaks its temp file
detail: run() reads the state, builds `previous`, then writeAtomic renames over the file. Two receipts recorded concurrently in the same repository (for example, two worktrees sharing the common dir, which hash to the same store) lose one writer's latest/previous entries. Separately, if writeFile or rename throws, the `<file>.<pid>.<rand>.tmp` file stays in the receipts dir, and the raw fs error surfaces instead of a KitExit.
fix_hint: Unlink the tmp file in a catch/finally and wrap the error in KitExit. Optionally take a lockfile (O_EXCL) around the read-modify-write.

title: Closing step requires a matching --threshold but not a matching --base
detail: The change id hashes the base. A receipt recorded without --base (merge-base with upstream, or root) and a check run with --base, or the reverse, never match. The check then reports 'only an earlier review exists, for a different version of this change', which misdescribes the situation and tells the user to re-run /w-review. The closing step only says to keep --threshold the same. Same text in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js:2262.
fix_hint: Say to pass the same --base (or none) to both receipt and check, or record the base in the receipt and report a base mismatch distinctly in decide().

title: --path-format=absolute (git >= 2.31) silently misbehaves on older git
detail: workingTree (line 215) and storeFile (line 314) call `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute ...`. Git before 2.31 (Ubuntu 20.04 ships 2.25, Debian 11 2.30, RHEL 8 2.27-2.31) does not know the option; rev-parse passes unknown flags through to stdout and exits 0 (verified: `git rev-parse --bogus=absolute --git-common-dir` prints `--bogus=absolute\n<path>`, rc 0). So `must()` returns a two-line string. In workingTree the index copy then fails with ENOENT, which line 219 swallows, so `git add -u` runs on an empty temp index and write-tree returns the empty tree: a dirty receipt would hash the wrong tree. storeFile then calls fs.realpath on the two-line string and every receipt and check exits 1 with a cryptic `ENOENT ... realpath '--path-format=absolute\n...'`. The gate is unusable on these hosts and the error does not say why. No test covers older git or a minimum version.
fix_hint: Drop --path-format and resolve the relative output of `--git-common-dir` / `--git-path index` with path.resolve against `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`'s cwd (or the cwd git ran in), or check `git --version` and throw a clear KitExit for < 2.31; do not swallow ENOENT on the index copy when status reported changes.

title: Stale-lock check compares local clock to filesystem mtime
detail: withLock treats the lock as stale when Date.now() - st.mtimeMs > staleMs. When the receipts dir lives on a network home directory (NFS/SMB), mtime comes from the server clock; with more than 30s of skew a live lock can be taken over, or a dead one never treated as stale until waitMs expires. Two concurrent receipts can then lose a `previous` entry.
fix_hint: Write the owner pid and a local timestamp into the lock file and judge staleness from that content (or from the pid being dead) instead of the server-set mtime.

title: Secrets-file lines keep surrounding whitespace, so a padded entry never matches
detail: parseSecretsFile strips only a trailing \r and pushes the line as is. A secrets file line like 'tok-abcdef  ' (trailing spaces from an editor or paste) becomes the secret 'tok-abcdef  ', and redactSecrets('x tok-abcdef y', ...) returns replaced: 0, so the value goes out unredacted with no warning. The same applies to fingerprints (the hash covers the spaces). Multi-line blocks already get trimmed lines as candidates; single-line entries do not.
fix_hint: Trim single-line entries (secrets.push(line.trim())) before applying MIN_LENGTH, and add a test with a padded entry.

title: Default secrets file is not found from a linked git worktree, so redaction silently does nothing
detail: The default path is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`/.claude/kit/secrets. In a linked worktree (the isolation marathon streams use), show-toplevel returns the worktree root. The secrets file is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. readFileOr(..., optional=true) returns null, and `redact` passes stdin through with replaced: 0 and no note. A user scrubbing text from inside a worktree gets back unredacted text that looks scrubbed.
fix_hint: Locate the main checkout through `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` (its parent directory) and use that as a fallback, or report in the output that no secrets file was found.

title: loadProjectSecrets doc says [] but the function returns null; nothing calls it
detail: The JSDoc says it returns [] when the file does not exist, but the code returns null. Nothing in the diff calls it: marathon's redactForModel parses the file on its own.
fix_hint: Return [] to match the doc, or fix the doc, or remove the unused export.

title: Secrets file that exists but cannot be reached is treated as 'no secrets' and fails open silently
detail: redactForModel gates on fileExists(), which returns false for any fs.access error, not only for a missing file. A dangling symlink (for example .claude/kit/secrets linked to a password store that is not mounted), EACCES on .claude/kit, or ELOOP all make review-brief skip redaction with no note, so the unredacted diff goes to the model and the brief says nothing. The kit CLI does the same: readFileOr treats ENOENT from a dangling symlink as 'missing default file' (verified: a dangling .claude/kit/secrets symlink gives {replaced: 0}, exit 0). The module promises the review-brief path fails closed on a broken secrets file, but these failures fail open.
fix_hint: Use fs.lstat (or check only e.code === 'ENOENT' on lstat) so 'the path exists in any form' blocks the brief; any other error, or a symlink whose target is missing, should stop with an error naming the path. In redact.js readFileOr, lstat before treating ENOENT as optional.

title: Secrets file present but kit missing: the diff goes out unredacted
detail: When .claude/kit/secrets exists, the user has said which values must not leave the machine. If the redact module cannot be imported (kit not installed, uninstalled, or redact.js/kit-exit.js missing, which the message check also swallows because the importer path contains 'redact.js'), review-brief still prints the whole raw diff and only adds a note at the end of the scope line. That note is easy to miss, and the secret has already gone out. The test locks in this fail-open behaviour instead of the fail-closed behaviour used for a malformed file.
fix_hint: When the secrets file exists and the redact module cannot load, fail the brief (or use a minimal inline exact-match redaction) rather than emit the unredacted diff; keep the 'works without kit' path only for when there is no secrets file.

title: Any git rev-parse failure is reported as 'not inside a git repository'
detail: secretsRoots maps every non-zero exit to 'not inside a git repository'. git older than 2.31 rejects --path-format=absolute, and running from inside .git rejects --show-toplevel. Both cases print a wrong diagnosis even though the user is in a repository.
fix_hint: Include a short, value-free summary of r.stderr in the message, or check for the specific 'not a git repository' text before using that wording.

title: Git older than 2.31 does not reject --path-format: it echoes it, and redaction silently fails open
detail: The new non-zero-status branch (lines 129-133, mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/redact.js) assumes git versions without --path-format fail with 'error: unknown option'. Real git rev-parse before 2.31 (Ubuntu 20.04 has 2.25, Debian 11 has 2.30, RHEL 8 ships 2.2x) does not do that. It passes unknown dash-arguments through show_flag, so it prints '--path-format=absolute' as its first output line and exits 0. secretsRoots then returns top='--path-format=absolute' (common is the toplevel path, whose basename is not .git). run() reads '--path-format=absolute/.claude/kit/secrets', resolved against process.cwd(), gets ENOENT, and readFileOr treats that as 'no secrets file'. The result is zero secrets and stdin passed through unredacted with exit 0. So on exactly the older environments the new diagnostic is meant for, the command leaks every secret instead of failing closed.
fix_hint: After a zero-status run, check that the output has exactly two lines and that both are absolute paths (path.isAbsolute(top) && !top.startsWith('-')). Otherwise throw a KitExit such as 'git >= 2.31 required (rev-parse --path-format); pass --secrets-file'. You could instead drop --path-format and resolve --show-toplevel and --git-common-dir against cwd yourself.

title: Old-git test fakes a stderr that real old git never produces
detail: The test stubs spawn to return status 128 with 'error: unknown option `path-format=absolute''. Real pre-2.31 git exits 0 and echoes the flag on stdout. The test therefore certifies a code path that never runs on old git, and it does not cover the fail-open case. It passes while the behaviour it names is wrong.
fix_hint:
Add a case with stub output { status: 0, stdout: '--path-format=absolute
/repo
.git
' } and assert that secretsRoots throws a KitExit and does not return a relative root.

title: 'all git versions print these relative to cwd' is not true for git < 2.13
detail: Before git 2.13, running rev-parse --git-common-dir and --git-path in a subdirectory printed the path relative to the top of the work tree, not to the cwd. Resolving that against cwd gives <sub>/.git. In push-gate the realpath or index copy then fails with a misleading error. In secretsRoots it adds a spurious extra root (<sub>). Both fail closed or are harmless, so no secret leaks, but the comment overstates what the code guarantees. The old-git test fake wraps modern git, so it cannot catch this.
fix_hint: Narrow the comment to git >= 2.13, or resolve the relative common-dir/git-path lines against --show-toplevel when the cwd-resolved path does not exist.

title: storeFile gets an undefined cwd when io.git has no .cwd and io.cwd is unset
detail: run() passes `git.cwd || io.cwd` to storeFile. changeId falls back to process.cwd() through its default parameter, but storeFile has no fallback, so gitPaths calls path.resolve(undefined, line) and throws a TypeError instead of a KitExit. This affects only programmatic callers, because the CLI always sets io.cwd.
fix_hint: Use `git.cwd || io.cwd || process.cwd()` in run() (or default the cwd parameter in storeFile/gitPaths).

title: rev-parse output error gives no next step and drops the caller's context
detail: When rev-parse exits 0 with odd output, resolveRevParse throws 'unexpected git rev-parse output (got N line(s), wanted M; first: ...)'. The `what` label gitPaths was given ('cannot find the index' / 'cannot find the git dir') is used only on a non-zero exit, and secretsRoots does not add its usual 'pass --secrets-file' remedy here. A user of redact or push-gate sees git internals with no action to take, unlike the neighbouring messages that name a fix.
fix_hint: Let the callers wrap or prefix the error: gitPaths prepends `what`, and secretsRoots appends '; pass --secrets-file' (optionally with a hint to check the git version).

title: Malformed-secrets failure is the only fail-closed message with no remedy
detail: The other new review-brief failures say 'refusing to emit an unredacted diff' and/or what to do (install the kit plugin or remove the secrets file). The malformed case says only '<rel> is malformed (<parser message>)'. The user is not told the brief was withheld on purpose or that fixing the file (for example closing the -----BEGIN block) unblocks it.
fix_hint: Use the same wording as the siblings: append ' — fix the file or remove it; refusing to emit an unredacted diff'.

title: A dangling secrets symlink is reported as a bare ENOENT
detail: This change deliberately treats a dangling symlink at the secrets path as an error. Yet redact reports 'cannot read secrets file <path>: ENOENT', and marathon (cli.js:705) reports 'cannot read .claude/kit/secrets (ENOENT)'. 'No such file' about a path the user can see with ls is confusing, and neither message says that the symlink target is missing or what to do (mount or restore the target, or remove the link).
fix_hint: When lstat succeeds but readFile gives ENOENT, say '<path> is a symlink to a missing target (<readlink>); restore it or remove the link'.

title: Lens step feeds `git diff HEAD`, which misses committed branch/PR work and untracked files
detail: /w-review is invoked as `/w-review [PR number or description]`, but the lens step always runs `git diff HEAD > /tmp/w-review.diff`. When the change under review is already committed (a PR or branch: the normal case), that diff is empty; brand-new files that are not yet `git add`ed are also left out. Traced in a temp repo: after committing a change that adds `await fetch(u)` to src/a.js and an `it(...)` test, `git diff HEAD | lenses --diff -` returns changed_files 0, fired [] and exit 0, so the reviewer records 'no lens applies' for a change that should fire missing-await and test-asserts-nothing. Same text is in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js (~line 2121).
fix_hint: Diff against the review base, e.g. `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD <base>)` (or `gh pr diff <N>` for a PR number), and include untracked files (`git add -N` or `git diff --no-index`); tell the reviewer to treat changed_files 0 as 'wrong input', not 'no findings'. Update the test regex in test/w-review-command.test.js to match.

title: Diff paths keep `c/`/`i/`/`w/` prefixes under diff.mnemonicPrefix, so directory-anchored globs silently miss
detail: The `diff --git` regex only recognises `a/` and `b/`, and cleanPath only strips `[ab]/`. The w-review step runs a bare `git diff HEAD`, which honours the user's diff.mnemonicPrefix (or diff.srcPrefix/dstPrefix) config. Traced: with `git -c diff.mnemonicPrefix=true diff HEAD | lenses --diff -` the reported files are `w/src/a.js` and `w/test/b.test.js`. Any glob containing a `/` is anchored at the root (`test/**/*.js`, `src/**/*.ts`, typical project lenses), so it never matches `w/test/...` and the lens silently does not fire, with exit 0. (Only basename globs like `**/*.js` survive.)
fix_hint: Pin the prefixes where the diff is produced (`git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ ...` in w-review.md and dot-shortcuts.js), and/or have the parser derive the path from the `+++`/`---` lines after stripping a single `[a-z]/` prefix that matches the diff --git header. Add a parseDiff test with mnemonic prefixes.

title: Empty or non-diff input is indistinguishable from 'no lens applies'
detail: If `--diff -` is run without a pipe (cli.js readStdin returns '' on a TTY), or `--diff` points at an empty or non-diff file, run() returns changed_files 0, fired [] and exits 0. Traced: `lenses --diff - < /dev/null` gives exit 0 with an empty result. A reviewer who mistypes the input or pipes the wrong thing gets a clean-looking 'nothing fired' instead of an error.
fix_hint: Fail with KitExit 1 when the input is non-empty but parses to zero files, and refuse `--diff -` when stdin is a TTY; or at minimum document in w-review that changed_files 0 means the input was wrong.
